87	=== ISSUE 143
88	## User Story
89	
90	As a maintainer reviewing a pull request that builds on another one, I want it to stay blocked until the pull request it depends on is actually merged, so that closing the earlier one without merging it cannot let unfinished work into the target branch.
91	
92	## User Scenario
93	Sam opens pull request #12, which uses an API that pull request #11 adds, and marks #12 as depending on #11 in the sidebar. A maintainer decides #11 needs a different approach and closes it without merging. Today, a closed #11 counts as done, so #12 can be merged and the target branch breaks.
94	
95	With this change, #12 stays blocked. Pressing Merge shows an error saying why, the API refuses to merge it, and a scheduled "merge when checks succeed" does not go through. Once #11 is reopened and merged, #12 can be merged as usual. Dependencies on issues work as they do today: closing the issue is enough.
96	
97	| #12 depends on | In state | Can #12 be merged? |
98	| --- | --- | --- |
99	| An issue | Open | No, as today |
100	| An issue | Closed | Yes, as today |
101	| A pull request | Open | No, as today |
102	| A pull request | Merged | Yes, as today |
103	| A pull request | Closed without merging | **No** (today: yes) |
104	
105	## Acceptance Criteria
106	- [ ] AC1: Given pull request B depends on pull request A, and A was closed without being merged, when a user with merge rights presses Merge on B, then B is not merged and the page shows "This pull request can't be merged until the pull requests it depends on are merged and the issues it depends on are closed."
107	- [ ] AC2: Given the same, when B is merged through the API, then the API answers 405 Method Not Allowed and B is not merged, as it does for the other reasons a pull request cannot be merged. Today it answers 500 Internal Server Error, for an open dependency too.
108	- [ ] AC3: Given the same, and B is scheduled to merge when its checks succeed, when B's checks succeed, then B is not merged and stays open.
109	- [ ] AC4: Given B depends on A, when A is merged, then B can be merged from the web and through the API, as today.
110	- [ ] AC5: Given B depends on an issue, when the issue is closed, then B can be merged, as today; while the issue is open, it cannot.
111	- [ ] AC6: Given B depends on A, and A was closed without being merged, when a user closes B, then B is closed, as today.
112	- [ ] AC7: Given a repository with "Enable Dependencies For Issues and Pull Requests" turned off in its settings, when a pull request whose dependencies are not resolved is merged, then it is merged, as closing an issue already ignores dependencies when the setting is off. Today the dependencies are hidden and cannot be removed, yet they still block the merge.
113	
114	## Out of Scope
115	- Showing on the pull request page which dependencies block it, and whether each one is open, merged or closed: Issue (#144)
116	- Dependency loops of three or more, and the checks the API skips when a dependency is added: Issue (#145)
117	- Merging a scheduled pull request the moment its last dependency merges. As today, it is tried again when its checks or reviews next change.
118	- Letting administrators merge past a dependency. "Merge anyway" does not skip dependencies today, and that stays.
119	- "Mark as manually merged", which records a merge made outside Gitea and does not check dependencies, as today.
120	- A separate setting for merge blocking. The existing "Enable Dependencies For Issues and Pull Requests" setting decides (AC7).
121	- Adding and removing dependencies, which Gitea already supports.
122	- Merge queues, and rebasing dependent pull requests automatically.
123	
124	## Open Questions
125	None
126

128	Added per commit during implementation, as in #53 and #54.
129	
130	## Scope
131	medium (3 points). Touches the rule that decides whether a dependency is resolved, and the three ways a pull request gets merged (the merge button, the API and a scheduled merge) with their error messages; a small change in each, plus tests for every path.

158	## Design Decision: Commit 1 - @ab-wm
159	### Decision 1: Merging gets its own dependency rule, and closing keeps the old one
160	
161	**Decision:** A new rule decides whether a pull request's dependencies let it be merged: every issue it depends on is closed, and every pull request it depends on is merged. Closing a pull request or an issue still uses the existing rule, where closed is enough (AC6).
162	**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Add a "for merging" switch to the existing rule. (b) Change the existing rule itself.
163	**Rationale:** Gitea keeps each reason a pull request can't be merged as its own small rule, so a separate dependency rule for merging follows that. (a) would make every place that closes an issue carry a switch it never turns on. (b) would also stop a user from closing a pull request whose dependency was closed without merging, which AC6 keeps working, and would change how issues close too.
164	**Consequences:** The two rules can drift apart if one is changed later without the other, so the new rule's description says how it differs from the closing one.
165	
166	--- ab-wm 2026-11-05T03:39:23Z
167	## Design Decision: Commit 3 - @ab-wm
168	### Decision 2: The merge button gets its own message for dependencies
169	
170	**Decision:** Pressing Merge on a pull request that its dependencies hold back shows a new message: "This pull request can't be merged until the pull requests it depends on are merged and the issues it depends on are closed." (AC1). It sits with the other reasons the merge button gives for not merging.
171	**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Rewrite the text of the existing message, "You need to close all issues that are blocking this pull request before you can merge it."
172	**Rationale:** The existing message is also shown when someone tries to close a pull request that still has open dependencies, where a sentence about merging would be wrong. Each of Gitea's other merge refusals has a message of its own, and this follows them.
173	**Consequences:** Other languages show the English sentence until it is translated on Crowdin. The old message stays in use for blocked closing, unchanged.
174	--- ab-wm 2026-11-05T03:43:15Z
175	## Commit 4 Design Decision - @ab-wm
176	### Decision 3: The API gives the same reason as the merge button
177	
178	**Decision:** When the API refuses a merge because of dependencies, it answers 405 Method Not Allowed (AC2) with the same sentence the merge button shows: "This pull request can't be merged until the pull requests it depends on are merged and the issues it depends on are closed."
179	**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A short phrase in the style of some of the API's other refusals, such as "Work in progress PRs cannot be merged".
180	**Rationale:** Someone who meets the refusal in a script reads the same reason as someone on the page, and the sentence says what has to happen first. The API's other refusals follow no single style: some give a short fixed phrase, others pass on the internal error's text, so neither choice breaks a pattern.
181	**Consequences:** The sentence now lives in two places, the English translations and the API code, so a wording change has to be made in both. Like the API's other refusals, it is not translated.

```text
@@ -199,3 +201,19 @@ func IssueNoDependenciesLeft(ctx context.Context, issue *Issue) (bool, error) {
 
 	return !exists, err
 }
+
+// MergeBlockedByDependencies checks if pr depends on an open issue or on a pull request that is not merged.
+// Closing ignores whether a pull request was merged (IssueNoDependenciesLeft); merging must not.
+func MergeBlockedByDependencies(ctx context.Context, pr *PullRequest) (bool, error) {
+	return db.GetEngine(ctx).
+		Table("issue_dependency").
+		Select("issue.*").
+		Join("INNER", "issue", "issue.id = issue_dependency.dependency_id").
+		Join("LEFT", "pull_request", "pull_request.issue_id = issue.id").
+		Where("issue_dependency.issue_id = ?", pr.IssueID).
+		And(builder.Or(
+			builder.Eq{"issue.is_closed": false},
+			builder.Eq{"pull_request.has_merged": false}, // NULL for an issue, so only a pull request matches
+		)).
+		Exist(&Issue{})
+}

+func TestMergeBlockedByDependencies(t *testing.T) {
+	// pull request 2 (issue 3, repo1) gets one dependency, depID, closed first when closeDep is set
+	setup := func(t *testing.T, depID int64, closeDep bool) *issues_model.PullRequest {
+		require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
+		doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 1})
+		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2})
+		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
+		dep := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: depID})
+		if closeDep {
+			_, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), dep, doer, issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{})
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+		}
+		require.NoError(t, issues_model.CreateIssueDependency(t.Context(), doer, pr.Issue, dep))
+		return pr
+	}
+	assertBlocked := func(t *testing.T, pr *issues_model.PullRequest, expected bool) {
+		blocked, err := issues_model.MergeBlockedByDependencies(t.Context(), pr)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		assert.Equal(t, expected, blocked)
+	}

+	t.Run("MergedPull", func(t *testing.T) {

+		// closing pr itself still treats the closed pull request as done
+		noDeps, err := issues_model.IssueNoDependenciesLeft(t.Context(), pr.Issue)

+	})
+}

+func TestCheckPullMergeableDependencies(t *testing.T) {
+	// user2 owns repo1 and could merge pull request 2, which gets one dependency, depID, closed first when closeDep is set
+	check := func(t *testing.T, depID int64, closeDep, dependenciesEnabled bool) error {
+		require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
+		ctx := t.Context()
+		doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
+		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2})
+		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(ctx))
+		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadBaseRepo(ctx))
+
+		dep := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: depID})
+		if closeDep {
+			_, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(ctx, dep, doer, issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{})
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+		}
+		require.NoError(t, issues_model.CreateIssueDependency(ctx, doer, pr.Issue, dep))
+
+		issuesUnit, err := pr.BaseRepo.GetUnit(ctx, unit.TypeIssues)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		issuesUnit.IssuesConfig().EnableDependencies = dependenciesEnabled // fixture repos leave it unset, which reads as off
+		require.NoError(t, repo_model.UpdateRepoUnitConfig(ctx, issuesUnit))
+
+		pr = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2}) // reload, so the setting comes from the database
+		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadBaseRepo(ctx))
+		perm, err := access_model.GetDoerRepoPermission(ctx, pr.BaseRepo, doer)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		return CheckPullMergeable(ctx, doer, &perm, pr, MergeCheckTypeGeneral, repo_model.MergeStyleMerge, false)
+	}
+
+	t.Run("OpenIssue", func(t *testing.T) {
+		assert.ErrorIs(t, check(t, 1, false, true), ErrDependenciesLeft)
+	})
+	t.Run("ClosedIssue", func(t *testing.T) {
+		assert.NoError(t, check(t, 1, true, true))
+	})
+	t.Run("PullClosedWithoutMerging", func(t *testing.T) {
+		assert.ErrorIs(t, check(t, 11, true, true), ErrDependenciesLeft) // pull request 5
+	})
+	t.Run("MergedPull", func(t *testing.T) {
+		assert.NoError(t, check(t, 2, true, true)) // pull request 1 is merged; closed as a real merge would, the fixture leaves it open
+	})

+		assert.NoError(t, check(t, 11, true, false))
+	})
+}

+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package integration
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"net/http"
+	"net/url"
+	"strconv"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	auth_model "gitea.dev/models/auth"
+	git_model "gitea.dev/models/git"
+	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
+	pull_model "gitea.dev/models/pull"
+	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
+	unit_model "gitea.dev/models/unit"
+	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
+	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/commitstatus"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/gitrepo"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/queue"
+	api "gitea.dev/modules/structs"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/test"
+	"gitea.dev/services/automerge"
+	"gitea.dev/services/forms"
+	issue_service "gitea.dev/services/issue"
+	commitstatus_service "gitea.dev/services/repository/commitstatus"
+	"gitea.dev/tests"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+func setDependenciesEnabled(t *testing.T, repoID int64, enabled bool) {
+	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: repoID})
+	issuesUnit, err := repo.GetUnit(t.Context(), unit_model.TypeIssues)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	issuesUnit.IssuesConfig().EnableDependencies = enabled
+	require.NoError(t, repo_model.UpdateRepoUnitConfig(t.Context(), issuesUnit))
+}
+
+// preparePullBlockedByClosedPull makes pull request 2 (#3 in user2/repo1) depend on pull request 5 (#5),
+// closes #5 without merging it, and waits until #3 is mergeable
+func preparePullBlockedByClosedPull(t *testing.T) (owner *user_model.User, pr *issues_model.PullRequest) {
+	owner = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
+	pr = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2})
+	require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
+	dep := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 11})
+
+	setDependenciesEnabled(t, pr.BaseRepoID, true) // fixture repos leave it unset, which reads as off
+	require.NoError(t, issues_model.CreateIssueDependency(t.Context(), owner, pr.Issue, dep))
+	require.NoError(t, issue_service.CloseIssue(t.Context(), dep, owner, ""))
+
+	// while #3 is being rechecked a merge is refused as "not ready", not for the dependency
+	require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
+		return unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: pr.ID}).Status == issues_model.PullRequestStatusMergeable
+	}, 5*time.Second, 50*time.Millisecond)
+	return owner, pr
+}
+
+func TestPullMergeBlockedByDependency(t *testing.T) {
+	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
+	owner, pr := preparePullBlockedByClosedPull(t)
+
+	session := loginUser(t, owner.Name)
+	req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/pulls/%d/merge", pr.Index), map[string]string{"do": string(repo_model.MergeStyleMerge)})
+	resp := session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusBadRequest)
+	assert.Equal(t, "This pull request can't be merged until the pull requests it depends on are merged and the issues it depends on are closed.", test.ParseJSONError(resp.Body.Bytes()).ErrorMessage)
+	assert.False(t, unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: pr.ID}).HasMerged)
+}
+
+func TestAPIMergePullBlockedByDependency(t *testing.T) {
+	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
+	owner, pr := preparePullBlockedByClosedPull(t)
+
+	token := getUserToken(t, owner.Name, auth_model.AccessTokenScopeWriteRepository)
+	req := NewRequestWithJSON(t, http.MethodPost, fmt.Sprintf("/api/v1/repos/user2/repo1/pulls/%d/merge", pr.Index), &forms.MergePullRequestForm{
+		Do: string(repo_model.MergeStyleMerge),
+	}).AddTokenAuth(token)
+	resp := MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
+	assert.Equal(t, "This pull request can't be merged until the pull requests it depends on are merged and the issues it depends on are closed.", DecodeJSON(t, resp, &api.APIError{}).Message)
+	assert.False(t, unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: pr.ID}).HasMerged)
+}
+
+func TestPullAutoMergeBlockedByDependency(t *testing.T) {
+	onGiteaRun(t, func(t *testing.T, u *url.URL) {
+		owner, pr := preparePullBlockedByClosedPull(t)
+		scheduled, err := automerge.ScheduleAutoMerge(t.Context(), owner, pr, repo_model.MergeStyleMerge, "auto merge test", false)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		require.True(t, scheduled)
+
+		baseRepo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: pr.BaseRepoID})
+		gitRepo, err := gitrepo.OpenRepository(t.Context(), baseRepo)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		sha, err := gitRepo.GetRefCommitID(pr.GetGitHeadRefName())
+		gitRepo.Close()
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		checksSucceed := func(statusContext string) { // then waits until the scheduled merge has run
+			require.NoError(t, commitstatus_service.CreateCommitStatus(t.Context(), baseRepo, owner, sha, &git_model.CommitStatus{
+				State:   commitstatus.CommitStatusSuccess,
+				Context: statusContext,
+			}))
+			require.NoError(t, queue.GetManager().FlushAll(t.Context(), 5*time.Second))
+		}
+
+		checksSucceed("ci/first")
+		assert.False(t, unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: pr.ID}).HasMerged)
+		assert.False(t, unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: pr.IssueID}).IsClosed)
+		unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &pull_model.AutoMerge{PullID: pr.ID}) // still scheduled, so it is tried again on the next change
+
+		// with dependencies turned off the same scheduled merge goes through, so only the dependency stopped it above
+		setDependenciesEnabled(t, pr.BaseRepoID, false)
+		checksSucceed("ci/second")
+		assert.True(t, unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: pr.ID}).HasMerged)
+	})
+}
+
+func TestPullCloseWithUnmergedDependency(t *testing.T) {
+	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
+	owner, pr := preparePullBlockedByClosedPull(t)
+
+	testIssueClose(t, loginUser(t, owner.Name), owner.Name, "repo1", strconv.FormatInt(pr.Index, 10))
+	assert.True(t, unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: pr.IssueID}).IsClosed)
+}
```

```text
1	---
2	scope: services/pull, services/gitdiff, services/automerge, services/automergequeue, services/agit
3	verified-at: c0092050a4
4	---
5	
6	# services/pull and services/gitdiff — pull requests, review, diffs
7	
8	**Read when:** touching PR creation, mergeability, merging, code review comments, or the diff
9	viewer.
10	**Not here:** the `PullRequest` row -> `models-issues.md`; issue-side logic -> `services-issue.md`.
11	
12	## Responsibilities
13	
14	| Package | Owns |
15	| --- | --- |
16	| `services/pull` | PR lifecycle: create, mergeability checking, merge, review, code comments, branch protection enforcement |
17	| `services/gitdiff` | parsing a git patch into the structures the diff viewer renders |
18	| `services/automerge`, `services/automergequeue` | "merge when checks pass" |
19	| `services/agit` | AGit flow — creating a PR by pushing a magic ref |
20	
21	## Key files
22	
23	| Path | What it holds |
24	| --- | --- |
25	| `services/pull/pull.go` | `NewPullRequest`, `ChangeTargetBranch`, `AddTestPullRequestTask`, `PushToBaseRepo`, `UpdateRef` |
26	| `services/pull/merge.go` | `Merge`, `SetMerged`, `MergedManually`, `IsUserAllowedToMerge`, `CheckPullBranchProtections`, `GetDefaultMergeMessage` |
27	| `services/pull/merge_merge.go`, `merge_squash.go`, `merge_rebase.go`, `merge_ff_only.go` | one file per merge style |
28	| `services/pull/check.go` | the mergeability queue: `AddPullRequestToCheckQueue`, `InitializePullRequests` |
29	| `services/pull/merge_tree.go` | conflict detection via `git merge-tree` |
30	| `services/pull/temp_repo.go` | `createTemporaryRepoForPR` — the scratch clone merges run in |
31	| `services/pull/patch.go` | `DownloadDiffOrPatch`, `AttemptThreeWayMerge`, `CheckFileProtection` |
32	| `services/pull/review.go` | `CreateCodeComment`, `SubmitReview`, `DismissReview`, `InvalidateCodeComments` |
33	| `services/pull/protected_branch.go` | `CreateOrUpdateProtectedBranch` |
34	| `services/gitdiff/gitdiff.go` | `Diff`, `DiffFile`, `DiffSection`, `DiffLine`, `ParsePatch`, `GetDiffForRender`, `GetDiffForAPI` |
35	| `services/gitdiff/gitdiff_excerpt.go` | expanding context lines in the viewer |
36	| `services/gitdiff/highlightdiff.go` | intra-line highlighting |
37	
38	## Conventions & invariants
39	
40	- **Mergeability is computed asynchronously.** Nothing recomputes it inline: a change pushes the PR
41	  id onto the worker queue in `check.go` via `AddPullRequestToCheckQueue`, and the result is
42	  written back to `PullRequest.Status`. The queue is unique-keyed, so pushing the same id twice is
43	  free. Code that needs a fresh answer must handle "not computed yet" rather than blocking.
44	- Merges do not run in the live repository. `createTemporaryRepoForPR` builds a scratch clone and
45	  the merge-style files operate there; only on success is the result pushed. A merge path that
46	  writes to the real repo directly is a bug.
47	- Merge styles are `repo_model.MergeStyle` values (`MergeStyleMerge`, `MergeStyleRebase`,
48	  `MergeStyleRebaseMerge`, `MergeStyleSquash`, `MergeStyleFastForwardOnly`) and each must be
49	  allowed by the repo's PR unit config — check with the unit accessors
50	  (`models-repo-and-git.md`), never by string comparison.
51	- `Merge` is not the permission check. `IsUserAllowedToMerge` and `CheckPullBranchProtections` sit
52	  beside it in `merge.go` but are separate calls the caller must make itself.
53	- **Review comments are anchored to a commit, not to a line of the current head.** `CreateCodeComment`
54	  takes `latestCommitID` and a `treePath`; when the branch moves, `InvalidateCodeComments` marks
55	  the ones that no longer apply. A comment feature that stores only a line number will drift.
56	- `GetDiffForRender` and `GetDiffForAPI` are deliberately separate — the render path carries
57	  highlighting, escaping and a repo link for building URLs. Do not use the API one to build HTML.
58	- `notify_service.*` is called after the transaction, exactly as in `services-issue.md`.
59	
60	## Recipes
61	
62	**Add something to the diff viewer.** Extend `DiffFile`/`DiffSection`/`DiffLine` in
63	`services/gitdiff/gitdiff.go`, populate it in `ParsePatch` or `GetDiffForRender`, then render it in
64	the repo diff templates and wire the frontend behaviour (`frontend-js.md`).
65	
66	**Add a merge style.** A `MergeStyle` constant and its unit-config flag in `models/repo`, a
67	`merge_<style>.go` implementation, a branch in `Merge`, the repo settings UI, and the locale keys.
68	
69	**Change when a PR becomes mergeable.** The check itself is in `check.go` / `merge_tree.go`. Add
70	the trigger by calling `AddPullRequestToCheckQueue`, not by computing inline.
71	
72	## Gotchas
73	
74	- `services/pull` is the logic; the `PullRequest` *rows* are in `models/issues/pull.go`. The
75	  package named `models/pull` is only automerge and review state (`models-issues.md`).
76	- A PR's issue fields (title, labels, comments) go through `services/issue`. Only PR-specific
77	  behaviour lives here, so a "PR change" often touches both packages.
78	- `AddTestPullRequestTask` reads as a test helper. It is production code that queues PR rechecks
79	  after a push.
80	- Diff size is capped by the `maxLines` / `maxFiles` arguments to `ParsePatch`; a large diff is
81	  truncated rather than failing, so check the `Diff` flags before assuming completeness.
82	
83	## Related
84	
85	- `services-issue.md` — the shared issue behaviour and the notify convention
86	- `models-issues.md` — `PullRequest`, `Review`, `Comment`
87	- `services-repository.md` — the push path that triggers PR rechecks
88
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# WSL side of wsync: sync ~/gitea (test runner only) to a branch from the Windows Gitea folder, then run a command.
# Called from Windows Git Bash as: wsync [command...]   (see C:\Users\carso\bin\wsync)
# Usage here: wsync-wsl <branch> [command...]
set -e
export PATH="$HOME/.local/go/bin:$HOME/.local/node/bin:$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"
branch="$1"; shift
cd ~/gitea
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: ~/gitea has local edits (it should never be edited). Inspect with: git -C ~/gitea status"; exit 1
fi
git fetch -q win
git switch -q -C "$branch" "win/$branch"
echo "WSL ~/gitea now at $branch: $(git log --oneline -1)"
if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then echo "+ $*"; "$@"; fi
```

```text
159				return ErrNoPermissionToMerge
160			}
161

163				// if doer is doing "manually merge" (mark as merged manually), do not check anything

165			}
```

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs PR 146 checks in ~/gitea (already synced by wsync). Each step reports its own status and the run keeps going.
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.local/go/bin:$HOME/.local/node/bin:$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"
export CGO_ENABLED=0
cd ~/gitea || exit 1
step() {
  name="$1"; shift
  echo; echo "##### $name"; echo "+ $*"
  start=$(date +%s)
  "$@" 2>&1 | tail -n "${TAIL:-40}"
  rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
  echo "##### RESULT $name rc=$rc in $(( $(date +%s) - start ))s"
}
echo "HEAD: $(git log --oneline -1)"
go version
step build make build
step unit-new-models go test -count=1 -v -run '^(TestMergeBlockedByDependencies|TestCreateIssueDependency)$' ./models/issues/
step unit-new-pull go test -count=1 -v -run '^TestCheckPullMergeableDependencies$' ./services/pull/
step pkg-models-issues go test -count=1 ./models/issues/
step pkg-services-pull go test -count=1 ./services/pull/
step pkg-services-automerge go test -count=1 ./services/automerge/...
step pkg-services-issue go test -count=1 ./services/issue/
step pkg-routers-web-repo go test -count=1 ./routers/web/repo/
step pkg-routers-api-repo go test -count=1 ./routers/api/v1/repo/
TAIL=60 step integration-new make 'test-sqlite#^(TestPullMergeBlockedByDependency|TestAPIMergePullBlockedByDependency|TestPullAutoMergeBlockedByDependency|TestPullCloseWithUnmergedDependency)$'
TAIL=30 step integration-neighbours make 'test-sqlite#^(TestAPIIssueDependencies.*|TestPullMerge.*|TestAPIPullMerge.*|TestPullAutoMerge.*|TestAPIMergePull.*)$'
step context-docs ./.claude-students/check.sh
echo; echo "##### ALL DONE"
```

```text
import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import {apiCreateRepo, apiCreateIssue, apiCreateUser, apiDeleteUser, apiUserHeaders, loginUser, randomString} from './utils.ts';

test('mark selected notifications as read in one action', async ({page, request}) => {
  const owner = `e2e-notif-${randomString(8)}`; // a fresh user, so no other test's notifications are listed
  const repo = 'notified';
  await apiCreateUser(request, owner);
  await apiCreateRepo(request, {name: repo, headers: apiUserHeaders(owner)});
  // the admin's issues notify the owner, who watches their own repo
  await Promise.all([
    apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo, title: 'First bulk notification'}),
    apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo, title: 'Second bulk notification'}),
    loginUser(page, owner),
  ]);

  const rows = page.locator('#notification_table .notifications-item');
  await expect(async () => { // notifications are written by a background queue
    await page.goto('/notifications');
    await expect(rows).toHaveCount(2, {timeout: 500});
  }).toPass();

  const bulkActions = page.locator('.notification-bulk-actions');
  await expect(bulkActions).toBeHidden();
  await rows.locator('.notification-checkbox').first().check();
  await rows.locator('.notification-checkbox').last().check();
  await expect(bulkActions).toContainText('2 selected');

  await Promise.all([
    page.waitForResponse((response) => response.url().includes('/notifications/bulk')),
    bulkActions.getByRole('button', {name: 'Mark as read'}).click(),
  ]);
  await expect(page.locator('.flash-message')).toContainText('Marked 2 notifications as read.');
  await expect(rows).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(page.locator('.notification-bulk-bar')).toHaveCount(0);

  await apiDeleteUser(request, owner);
});
```

```cjs
// Simulated e2e run of PR #146 (issue #143) against the local WSL Gitea instance.
// Expected values come from the ACs in issue #143, not from the branch's output.
// Run in WSL: E2E_USER=... E2E_PASS=... node pr146-e2e.cjs
const {chromium, request} = require('/home/carsonrackley/gitea/node_modules/@playwright/test');
const fs = require('node:fs');
const path = require('node:path');

const BASE = process.env.BASE || 'http://localhost:3001';
const USER = process.env.E2E_USER;
const PASS = process.env.E2E_PASS;
const OUT = process.env.OUT || path.join(__dirname, 'pr146-e2e');
const RUN = Date.now().toString(36).slice(-5);
const MSG = "This pull request can't be merged until the pull requests it depends on are merged and the issues it depends on are closed.";
fs.mkdirSync(OUT, {recursive: true});

const results = [];
function record(id, ac, name, expected, actual, pass) {
  results.push({id, ac, name, expected, actual, pass});
  console.log(`${pass ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'} ${id} [${ac}] ${name} | expected: ${expected} | actual: ${actual}`);
}

let api;
async function call(method, p, data) {
  const r = await api.fetch(`${BASE}/api/v1${p}`, {method, data});
  let body = null;
  try { body = await r.json(); } catch { body = null; }
  return {status: r.status(), body};
}
async function must(method, p, data, ok = [200, 201, 204]) {
  const r = await call(method, p, data);
  if (!ok.includes(r.status)) throw new Error(`${method} ${p} -> ${r.status} ${JSON.stringify(r.body)}`);
  return r.body;
}
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, ms));

async function createRepo(name, depsEnabled = true) {
  await must('POST', '/user/repos', {name, auto_init: true, default_branch: 'main'});
  await setDeps(name, depsEnabled);
  return name;
}
async function setDeps(repo, enabled) {
  await must('PATCH', `/repos/${USER}/${repo}`, {internal_tracker: {enable_time_tracker: true, allow_only_contributors_to_track_time: true, enable_issue_dependencies: enabled}});
}
async function makePR(repo, branch, title) {
  await must('POST', `/repos/${USER}/${repo}/contents/${branch}.txt`, {content: Buffer.from(`${branch}\n`).toString('base64'), branch: 'main', new_branch: branch, message: `add ${branch}`});
  const pr = await must('POST', `/repos/${USER}/${repo}/pulls`, {head: branch, base: 'main', title});
  return pr.number;
}
async function makeIssue(repo, title) {
  return (await must('POST', `/repos/${USER}/${repo}/issues`, {title})).number;
}
async function addDep(repo, index, depRepo, depIndex) {
  await must('POST', `/repos/${USER}/${repo}/issues/${index}/dependencies`, {owner: USER, repo: depRepo, index: depIndex});
}
async function setState(repo, index, state, kind = 'pulls') {
  await must('PATCH', `/repos/${USER}/${repo}/${kind}/${index}`, {state});
}
async function getPull(repo, index) {
  return must('GET', `/repos/${USER}/${repo}/pulls/${index}`);
}
async function waitMergeable(repo, index, timeout = 30000) {
  const end = Date.now() + timeout;
  while (Date.now() < end) {
    const pr = await getPull(repo, index);
    if (pr.mergeable) return pr;
    await sleep(300);
  }
  throw new Error(`${repo}#${index} never became mergeable`);
}
async function apiMerge(repo, index, extra = {}) {
  return call('POST', `/repos/${USER}/${repo}/pulls/${index}/merge`, {Do: 'merge', ...extra});
}

async function uiMerge(page, repo, index, shot) {
  await page.goto(`${BASE}/${USER}/${repo}/pulls/${index}`);
  await page.locator('.merge-button > button.ui.button').first().click();
  const [resp] = await Promise.all([
    page.waitForResponse((r) => r.url().endsWith(`/pulls/${index}/merge`) && r.request().method() === 'POST'),
    page.locator('form.form-fetch-action button[name="do"]').click(),
  ]);
  let toast = '';
  if (resp.status() >= 400) {
    const t = page.locator('.toastify.on').first();
    await t.waitFor({timeout: 5000}).catch(() => {});
    toast = (await t.textContent().catch(() => '')) || '';
  }
  await page.screenshot({path: path.join(OUT, `${shot}.png`), fullPage: true});
  return {status: resp.status(), toast: toast.trim()};
}

async function step(id, ac, name, fn) {
  try {
    await fn();
  } catch (err) {
    record(id, ac, name, 'no error', `ERROR: ${err.message.split('\n')[0]}`, false);
  }
}

(async () => {
  if (!USER || !PASS) throw new Error('set E2E_USER and E2E_PASS');
  api = await request.newContext({extraHTTPHeaders: {Authorization: `Basic ${Buffer.from(`${USER}:${PASS}`).toString('base64')}`}});
  const browser = await chromium.launch();
  const page = await (await browser.newContext({viewport: {width: 1280, height: 900}})).newPage();
  const login = await page.request.post(`${BASE}/user/login`, {form: {user_name: USER, password: PASS}, maxRedirects: 0});
  if (![302, 303].includes(login.status())) throw new Error(`login failed: ${login.status()}`);

  // --- main repo: A is the dependency; B, C, D depend on A; E depends on issue I
  const main = await createRepo(`pr146-deps-${RUN}`);
  const A = await makePR(main, 'feature-a', 'A: prerequisite change');
  const B = await makePR(main, 'feature-b', 'B: depends on A (merge from web)');
  const C = await makePR(main, 'feature-c', 'C: depends on A (merge through API)');
  const D = await makePR(main, 'feature-d', 'D: depends on A (gets closed)');
  const E = await makePR(main, 'feature-e', 'E: depends on issue I');
  const I = await makeIssue(main, 'I: prerequisite issue');
  for (const n of [B, C, D]) await addDep(main, n, main, A);
  await addDep(main, E, main, I);
  for (const n of [A, B, C, D, E]) await waitMergeable(main, n);

  await step('E01', 'AC2', 'API merge while the dependency PR is still open', async () => {
    const r = await apiMerge(main, C);
    const merged = (await getPull(main, C)).merged;
    record('E01', 'AC2', 'API merge while the dependency PR is still open', '405 + message, not merged (was 500)', `${r.status} "${r.body?.message}" merged=${merged}`, r.status === 405 && r.body?.message === MSG && !merged);
  });

  await setState(main, A, 'closed'); // A closed without merging
  for (const n of [B, C, D]) await waitMergeable(main, n);

  await step('E02', 'AC1', 'Web merge button while A is closed without merging', async () => {
    const r = await uiMerge(page, main, B, 'E02-web-merge-refused');
    const merged = (await getPull(main, B)).merged;
    record('E02', 'AC1', 'Web merge button while A is closed without merging', `refused, toast "${MSG}", not merged`, `HTTP ${r.status}, toast "${r.toast}", merged=${merged}`, r.status >= 400 && r.toast.includes(MSG) && !merged);
  });
  await step('E03', 'AC2', 'API merge while A is closed without merging', async () => {
    const r = await apiMerge(main, B);
    const merged = (await getPull(main, B)).merged;
    record('E03', 'AC2', 'API merge while A is closed without merging', '405 + message, not merged', `${r.status} "${r.body?.message}" merged=${merged}`, r.status === 405 && r.body?.message === MSG && !merged);
  });
  await step('E04', 'Out of scope', 'API "merge anyway" (force_merge) by the repo owner', async () => {
    const r = await apiMerge(main, B, {force_merge: true});
    const merged = (await getPull(main, B)).merged;
    record('E04', 'Out of scope', 'API "merge anyway" (force_merge) by the repo owner', '405, still blocked (issue: "Merge anyway" does not skip dependencies)', `${r.status} merged=${merged}`, r.status === 405 && !merged);
  });
  await step('E05', 'Edge', 'Scheduling "merge when checks succeed" while blocked', async () => {
    const r = await apiMerge(main, B, {merge_when_checks_succeed: true});
    const merged = (await getPull(main, B)).merged;
    record('E05', 'Edge', 'Scheduling "merge when checks succeed" while blocked', 'refused (405) or scheduled, never merged', `${r.status} "${r.body?.message ?? ''}" merged=${merged}`, !merged);
  });
  await step('E06', 'AC6', 'Close D from the web while A is closed without merging', async () => {
    await page.goto(`${BASE}/${USER}/${main}/pulls/${D}`);
    await Promise.all([
      page.waitForResponse((r) => r.url().includes(`/issues/${D}/comments`) || r.url().includes('/comments'), {timeout: 10000}).catch(() => null),
      page.locator('#status-button').click(),
    ]);
    await sleep(1000);
    await page.screenshot({path: path.join(OUT, 'E06-close-d.png'), fullPage: true});
    const pr = await getPull(main, D);
    record('E06', 'AC6', 'Close D from the web while A is closed without merging', 'D closed, not merged', `state=${pr.state} merged=${pr.merged}`, pr.state === 'closed' && !pr.merged);
  });
  await step('E07', 'AC5', 'API merge of E while issue I is open', async () => {
    const r = await apiMerge(main, E);
    record('E07', 'AC5', 'API merge of E while issue I is open', '405, not merged', `${r.status} merged=${(await getPull(main, E)).merged}`, r.status === 405);
  });
  await step('E08', 'AC5', 'API merge of E after issue I is closed', async () => {
    await setState(main, I, 'closed', 'issues');
    await waitMergeable(main, E);
    const r = await apiMerge(main, E);
    record('E08', 'AC5', 'API merge of E after issue I is closed', '200, merged', `${r.status} merged=${(await getPull(main, E)).merged}`, r.status === 200 && (await getPull(main, E)).merged);
  });

  // AC4: reopen and merge A, then B (web) and C (API) go through
  await step('E09', 'AC4', 'Reopen and merge A', async () => {
    await setState(main, A, 'open');
    await waitMergeable(main, A);
    const r = await apiMerge(main, A);
    record('E09', 'AC4', 'Reopen and merge A', '200, merged', `${r.status} merged=${(await getPull(main, A)).merged}`, r.status === 200);
  });
  await step('E10', 'AC4', 'Web merge of B once A is merged', async () => {
    await waitMergeable(main, B);
    const r = await uiMerge(page, main, B, 'E10-web-merge-after-a');
    await sleep(500);
    const merged = (await getPull(main, B)).merged;
    record('E10', 'AC4', 'Web merge of B once A is merged', 'merged', `HTTP ${r.status} toast="${r.toast}" merged=${merged}`, merged);
  });
  await step('E11', 'AC4', 'API merge of C once A is merged', async () => {
    await waitMergeable(main, C);
    const r = await apiMerge(main, C);
    record('E11', 'AC4', 'API merge of C once A is merged', '200, merged', `${r.status} merged=${(await getPull(main, C)).merged}`, r.status === 200);
  });

  // AC7: dependencies turned off in the repository settings
  const off = await createRepo(`pr146-off-${RUN}`);
  const G = await makePR(off, 'feature-g', 'G: dependency, closed without merging');
  const F = await makePR(off, 'feature-f', 'F: depends on G');
  await addDep(off, F, off, G);
  await setState(off, G, 'closed');
  await waitMergeable(off, F);
  await step('E12', 'AC7', 'Control: F blocked while dependencies are on', async () => {
    const r = await apiMerge(off, F);
    record('E12', 'AC7', 'Control: F blocked while dependencies are on', '405', `${r.status}`, r.status === 405);
  });
  await step('E13', 'AC7', 'Web merge of F with dependencies turned off', async () => {
    await setDeps(off, false);
    const repo = await must('GET', `/repos/${USER}/${off}`);
    const r = await uiMerge(page, off, F, 'E13-web-merge-deps-off');
    await sleep(500);
    const merged = (await getPull(off, F)).merged;
    record('E13', 'AC7', 'Web merge of F with dependencies turned off', 'merged', `setting=${repo.internal_tracker?.enable_issue_dependencies} HTTP ${r.status} merged=${merged}`, merged);
  });

  // AC3: a scheduled merge whose dependency is closed without merging after it was scheduled
  const auto = await createRepo(`pr146-auto-${RUN}`);
  const J = await makePR(auto, 'feature-j', 'J: dependency, closed without merging');
  const H = await makePR(auto, 'feature-h', 'H: scheduled to merge when checks succeed');
  const hPR = await waitMergeable(auto, H);
  await must('POST', `/repos/${USER}/${auto}/statuses/${hPR.head.sha}`, {state: 'pending', context: 'ci/e2e'});
  await step('E14', 'AC3', 'Scheduled merge does not go through when checks succeed', async () => {
    const s = await apiMerge(auto, H, {merge_when_checks_succeed: true});
    if (s.status !== 201) throw new Error(`schedule -> ${s.status} ${JSON.stringify(s.body)}`);
    await addDep(auto, H, auto, J);
    await setState(auto, J, 'closed');
    await waitMergeable(auto, H);
    await must('POST', `/repos/${USER}/${auto}/statuses/${hPR.head.sha}`, {state: 'success', context: 'ci/e2e'});
    await sleep(5000);
    const pr = await getPull(auto, H);
    await page.goto(`${BASE}/${USER}/${auto}/pulls/${H}`);
    const stillScheduled = await page.locator('form[action$="/cancel_auto_merge"]').count() > 0;
    await page.screenshot({path: path.join(OUT, 'E14-scheduled-still-pending.png'), fullPage: true});
    record('E14', 'AC3', 'Scheduled merge does not go through when checks succeed', 'not merged, open, still scheduled', `merged=${pr.merged} state=${pr.state} scheduled=${stillScheduled}`, !pr.merged && pr.state === 'open' && stillScheduled);
  });

  // Edge: dependency on a pull request in another repository
  const cross = await createRepo(`pr146-cross-${RUN}`);
  const Z = await makePR(main, 'feature-z', 'Z: cross-repo dependency, closed without merging');
  const X = await makePR(cross, 'feature-x', 'X: depends on Z in another repo');
  await addDep(cross, X, main, Z);
  await setState(main, Z, 'closed');
  await waitMergeable(cross, X);
  await step('E15', 'Edge', 'Cross-repository dependency closed without merging', async () => {
    const r = await apiMerge(cross, X);
    record('E15', 'Edge', 'Cross-repository dependency closed without merging', '405, not merged', `${r.status} merged=${(await getPull(cross, X)).merged}`, r.status === 405);
  });

  await browser.close();
  const summary = {run: RUN, base: BASE, repos: [main, off, auto, cross], passed: results.filter((r) => r.pass).length, total: results.length, results};
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(OUT, `results-${RUN}.json`), JSON.stringify(summary, null, 2));
  console.log(`\nSUMMARY ${summary.passed}/${summary.total} passed; repos: ${summary.repos.join(', ')}`);
  process.exit(summary.passed === summary.total ? 0 : 1);
})().catch((err) => { console.error('FATAL', err); process.exit(2); });
```

with `unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean`; add fixture rows only if no existing row fits.

at the top of the test; drive it through HTTP the way the neighbouring tests do. Do not add a
`TestMain` — `integration_test.go` already owns it.
